name: UI
description: Retained mode and DOM-style API to render interactive user-interfaces, with a Solid.js-inspired UI framework built on top.
It's recommended to either use the out-of-the-box UI framework (or build your own) instead of working with the retained mode API directly.
Retained mode has been chosen to significantly reduce the overhead of communicating between Lua and the engine for mostly static UIs.

parameters.name: textContent
parameters.description: Initial text content of the element.

functions.name: createRichTextElement
functions.description: Creates a new rich text element designed for user input.

functions.name: getId
functions.description: Gets the unique ID for this element (can be used for equality).

functions.name: isTextElement
functions.description: Returns whether the given parameter is a text UI element.

returns.name: isTextElement
returns.description: Whether the value is a text element.

functions.name: isRichTextElement
functions.description: Returns whether the given parameter is a rich text UI element.

returns.name: isRichTextElement
returns.description: Whether the value is a rich text element.

functions.name: removeElement
functions.description: Removes the element from its parent. No-op if the element has no parent.

functions.name: appendElement
description: Appends an element to the end of another element's children.
Removes the child element from its current parent if it has one.

functions.name: getChildren
description: Returns a list of the element's children.
This is a copy, so will not update if the children of the element change
(nor will the element's children change if this list is modified).

functions.name: getElementName
functions.description: Returns the debug name of the element.

functions.name: setElementName
functions.description: Sets the debug name of the element.

functions.name: getTextContent
functions.description: Returns the contents of a text element.

functions.name: setTextContent
functions.description: Updates the contents of a text element.

functions.name: getNumLines
functions.description: Gets the number of lines in the rich text element (not including visual wrapping).

functions.name: getNumCharacters
functions.description: Gets the number of characters in the rich text element's line (not including visual wrapping).

parameters.name: line
parameters.description: Line to get the length of. Throws if out of range.

functions.name: setTokens
description: Overwrites a selection in the rich text element with the given tokens, splitting and merging tokens as needed.
Shifts the caret vertically if the number of lines to write is different to the number selected and the caret is after the selection.
Does not shift the caret within or before the selection. i.e. you must manually move the caret when applying user input.

functions.name: setCaret
functions.description: Sets the position of the caret within the rich text element, if the element is focused.

parameters.name: newCaret
parameters.description: [line, character] of the new caret position.

functions.name: getCaret
functions.description: Gets the position of the caret within the rich text element, or `nil` if the element isn't focused.

returns.name: caret
returns.description: [line, character] of the caret position, if focused.

functions.name: moveCaret
description: Moves the rich text element's caret the given number of lines and characters, if the element is focused.
Vertical caret movement maintains the horizontal pixel position of the caret as close as possible,
and preserves it across lines of varying lengths until the next horizontal movement.

parameters.name: delta
parameters.description: [line, character] deltas to move the caret in.

functions.name: setStyle
description: Sets a style on the element when in the specified state.
Styles are used in the order `Clicked -> Hovered -> Always -> Engine Defaults`.
The first state as per the order above which has a style set will be used.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Accepted type depends on the style being set.

parameters.name: when
parameters.description: In which state the style will be used.

functions.name: removeStyle
description: Removes the style from the element when in the specified state.
Styles are used in the order Clicked -> Hovered -> Always -> Engine Defaults.
Removing a style from one of the layers means the first set style in a lower state (as above) will be used instead.

parameters.name: when
parameters.description: In which state the style will be removed.

functions.name: isDebuggerEnabled
functions.description: Returns whether the Clay debugger is enabled.

functions.name: createComponent
description: Creates a component from the given function.
This sets up the component function as stateful and normalises its parameters.

parameters.name: children
parameters.description: Signal containing the child DOM elements of the component.

returns.name: elementsSignal
returns.description: Signal containing flattened DOM elements produced by the component.

functions.name: render
description: Resolves the component tree and appends all root nodes to the given element.
Should be called only once when initialising the UI.

returns.name: elementsSignal
returns.description: Signal containing flattened DOM elements produced by the component.

parameters.name: element
parameters.description: UI element to mount the components to.

functions.name: toString
description: Stringifies the element and its children into a format resembling HTML/XML
Useful for debugging and snapshot testing.

parameters.name: indent
parameters.description: Number of spaces to indent all lines by. Defaults to `0`.

events.name: pressed
events.description: Fires when the mouse or controller button bound to click is pressed on an element.

events.name: released
events.description: Fires when the mouse or controller button bound to click is released on an element.

events.name: textEntry
events.description: Fires when the user enters text into a rich text element.

events.name: keyPress
description: Fires when the user presses a key in a rich text element.
Note this won't necessarily match the actual text that would be entered by the key press (e.g. when using a non-Latin alphabet).
You should use the `'textEntry'` event for inserting typed characters into the element, and this event for special keys like backspace.

events.name: keyRepeat
description: Fires when the Operating System repeats a held key in a rich text element.
Note this won't necessarily match the actual text that would be entered by the key press (e.g. when using a non-Latin alphabet).
You should use the `'textEntry'` event for inserting typed characters into the element, and this event for special keys like backspace.

events.name: keyRelease
description: Fires when the user releases a key in a rich text element.
Note this won't necessarily match the actual text that would be entered by the key press (e.g. when using a non-Latin alphabet).
You should use the `'textEntry'` event for inserting typed characters into the element, and this event for special keys like backspace.

classes.name: RichTextToken
classes.description: An independently stylable chunk of text in a rich text element.

classes.name: RichTextTokenStyles
description: Styling properties for rich text tokens.
All properties are optional and will default to the values defined on the element.

enums.name: StyleMode
enums.description: When to apply a given style. Styles apply in the order `Clicked -> Hovered -> Always -> Engine Defaults`.

enums.name: SizeMode
description: Determines how the `Element` will respond to changes in width/height by its parent and children.
`FixedPercent` fixes the `Element`'s width/height to a percentage (0-1) of the parent's size,
using the first of `Width`, `MaxWidth` or `MinWidth` which is defined (and `*Height` for height).

enums.name: ChildAlignment
enums.description: Alignment of children on a given axis relative to this `Element`'s content box.

enums.name: Direction
enums.description: Direction that children are laid out in this `Element`.

enums.name: TextWrapping
enums.description: Where in the string it's valid to insert line breaks in order to prevent overflow.

enums.name: TextAlignment
enums.description: Alignment of `TextElement`s which are the immediate child of this `Element`.

enums.name: Display
enums.description: Determines the visibility of the element and its children.

enums.name: Overflow
enums.description: Visibility and scrolling behaviour of child content overflowing the content box.

constants.name: SCREEN
constants.description: Root DOM element rendered to the screen in 2D. Shared by all screenspace UI, so you'll want to further restrict/abstract this if exposed to addons in your game.
